s1.syndrome_frame: Cardiac arrest with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and hemodynamic collapse
salient_findings: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
key_facts: 34-year-old White woman with a history of obesity
Presented after an unwitnessed cardiac arrest
Developed atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response
Experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions
Triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and resultant hemodynamic collapse
Initial laboratory tests showed no electrolyte derangements
Elevated troponin T and troponin I levels
Urine toxicology, alcohol, and acetaminophen screening results were negative
ECG showed sinus tachycardia with heart rate 101 beats/min and QTc 443 ms
Transthoracic echocardiogram showed normal biventricular size and function
Diagnostic coronary angiogram showed no obstructive coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG showed QTc 443 ms, which is a risk factor for torsades de pointes and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular tachycardia and fibrillation, which can be associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had ventricular fibrillation without clear underlying cause

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a history of obesity and cardiac arrest, which can be associated with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient experienced frequent premature ventricular contractions triggering polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which is a hallmark of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). The absence of structural heart disease and normal cardiac function also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's QTc interval was mildly prolonged but not significantly long enough to be diagnostic of Long QT syndrome, and the presence of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is more suggestive of CPVT.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed normal biventricular size and function, with no evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: While the patient did experience ventricular fibrillation, the presence of a clear trigger (premature ventricular contractions) and the pattern of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia suggest a more specific diagnosis like CPVT.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The cardiac imaging studies showed no evidence of left ventricular hypertrophy or outflow tract obstruction, making this diagnosis unlikely.
